notes:
Need to search first.I couldn't write the notes. None of the research worked, so I have no sources to base them on.

My first attempt tried to open the commentary pages directly (Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub, and John Wesley's notes on studylight). The tool refused, because a page has to turn up in a search before it can be opened. My second attempt ran about 18 searches at the same time and hit the usage limit. That used up all my research tool calls for this turn, so I couldn't search or open anything.

Your rules say to report only what pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any verse notes, because none of them would have a page behind it.

If you ask again, I'll go more slowly, a few searches at a time, opening each page once it shows up. I'd work in this order:
1. **Standard reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, biblehub (Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary), Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** this mainly affects vv. 14–22: whether the "great tribulation" already happened when Jerusalem fell in AD 70, is still future, or both. I'd look at Ligonier and The Gospel Coalition (Reformed), Grace to You and Desiring God (Baptist), the Assemblies of God site and Enduring Word (Pentecostal), John Wesley's notes (Methodist), and LCMS and 1517 (Lutheran).
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey (modern scholarship), New Advent's Catena Aurea and Catholic Answers (Catholic), OCA (Orthodox).

To fit within the limits, I could also do it in parts, for example vv. 1–14 first and then vv. 15–26. Tell me which you'd prefer.
